newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower, feeders up at new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower, feeders up at new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed lower despite strong cash markets to end lower while feeder cattle again rose on strong cash to post some new contract highs, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.250 cent per lb lower to unchanged with June off most at 65.175 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.025 to 0.400 higher with August up most at 76.950 after posting a new high early of 77.000 cents. January and March also posted new highs.
Expectations that boxed beef prices as well as cash cattle markets were near tops weighed on live cattle futures.

Retailers should finish beef purchases for Memorial Day in the next few days and the next move in beef will likely ease until the next round of buying for Fathers Day promotions in mid-June. Packers are also seen buying cattle actively for the next week but their buying should slow when they have ensured enough supply to fill beef orders, traders said.

Choice heavy-weight boxed beef ran up another $1.32 per cwt at noon Tuesday to $108.70, the highest level since December 4, 1995, and choice cattle sold at $69 per cwt Wednesday, the higest price since late February.

But the outlook for increased fed cattle supplies prompted resistance. Previous Cattle-on-Feed reports indicated fed cattle supplies will increase going into June. The increase in market-ready cattle should keep beef prices in check even as retailers start shopping for beef for Fathers Day, typically one of the largest beef consumption days of the year, traders said.
"Any strength we get from time to time now until August is not going to come from supply - it has to come from demand," said Joe Kropf, of Kropf and Love Consulting.
"This holiday buying is generating some wholesale beef business - but it (next cattle report) should show plenty of (live) supply ahead," Kropf added.
Early indications on the next Cattle-on-Feed report point to larger on-feed supplies, traders added.

Refco, E.D.&F. Man and Prudential Securities bought early while R.J. O'Brien, Cargill Investor Services and ADM Investor Services sold, traders said. Rosenthal Collins sold June and August. In live cattle options, commission houses sold June 66 calls and ther was commercial hedging by doing risk reversals in October, buying 68 puts and selling 72 calls, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures ran up to new highs for the seventh time in eight days on buying prompted by a surging CME feeder cattle index and lower corn futures. Demand for feeders has remained strong following active feedlot movement and interest to put feeders on grass, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index jumped $1.21 to $73.34 per cwt, the highest level since February 16, 1995.
Feedlot profits have been better than expected "and that is keeping them coming back for feeder cattle," Kropf said.
Kropf and others also noted the active corn plantings which point to possible increased corn supplies at lower prices in the fall.
Refco, E.D.&F. Man and LIT division of First Options rolled long May positions into August. Cargill Investor Services bought August live cattle and sold May feeders early, pit sources said.
